feedback: Reject. The artifact is mechanically clean but encodes the wrong task. The stated task is a recurring obligation — at every moment the ball is out of the way, the key must be carried at that moment or picked up later (G(blocker_moved -> F has_door_key)) — with no requirement to open the door or collect the box. The candidate is the canonical move-ball -> get-key -> open-door -> pick-box chain. Concrete failures: (1) Fidelity: u2->u3 (+0.3 on door_open) and u3->u4 (+1.0 on target_picked_up) encode goals absent from the task, and the accepting state u4 is only reachable by completing them; a fully compliant agent that never opens the door earns 0.3 and never reaches a final state. (2) The maximally rewarding trace violates the task: the environment's own example trace drops the key at step 19 while the ball is out of the way and the door is open, never re-picks it, and picks up the box at step 28 — an unfulfilled obligation — yet the candidate pays the full 0.1+0.2+0.3+1.0 (key_lost is false with the door open, so u3 self-loops silently). A compliant box pickup requires putting the ball back in front of the door before dropping the key; the RM cannot distinguish the two, paying 1.6 for both. (3) Discharge trigger mis-scoped: u1->u2 requires blocker_moved & has_door_key in the same step, but an obligation survives even if the ball is put back first; a discharging key pickup with blocker_moved false earns nothing and strands progress in u1. A faithful RM discharges on has_door_key (ordering the has_door_key transition before the blocker_moved one). (4) Regression mis-scoped and incomplete: the only regression is u2->u1 on key_lost, which additionally requires the door closed. Dropping the key while the door is closed and the ball is back in front creates no obligation under the task yet costs -0.2 and forces a re-earning detour; conversely, dropping the key while the door is open and the ball is out of the way does create an obligation but is invisible to the RM (key_lost false, u3 absorbing), so the 'at every moment' recurrence is dropped entirely after u3. The task needs an explicit pending-obligation regression keyed to 'ball out of the way and key not carried', independent of door state. (5) Compactness: two states (no-pending / pending, oscillating on obligation creation and has_door_key discharge) suffice; the five-state chain is not minimal for this property. Positives worth keeping: exact paper format with a nonempty FINAL_STATES header; predicate-only events correctly using blocker_moved rather than the published RM's has_ball; per-state else self-loops covering irrelevant events; key_lost correctly handled as a one-step event; rewards bounded with no farming exploit (+0.1 fires once since u0 is never re-entered, the door cannot relock, the episode ends on +1.0); all states reachable through feasible events. Rewrite the transition structure around the pending-obligation semantics before resubmitting.

STATES: u0, u1
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_door_key) -> u0

(u1, has_door_key, u0) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. Semantic fidelity: the two-state automaton is the canonical encoding of the task's response property. u0->u1 fires exactly at moments where blocker_moved & !has_door_key holds (the 'not carrying the key then' case), opening a pending obligation penalized at -1.0; u1->u0 fires on any later has_door_key (the 'pick it up later' discharge, +1.0). Acceptance (ending in u0) is equivalent to G(blocker_moved -> F has_door_key): any undischarged 'pick it up later' commitment leaves the machine in u1 and is correctly rejected, and obligations opened while already pending are discharged by the same recovery, so acceptance and rejection sets match the stated task exactly. Persistent/event distinctions are handled correctly: blocker_moved and has_door_key are used with their condition (persistent) readings — dropping the key while the ball is out of the way re-enters u1 from u0, and re-dropping the ball in front of the door re-arms the obligation from u0 — while key_lost (an event) is rightly unused and, together with door_open and target_picked_up, is absorbed by the per-state else self-loops, covering all irrelevant events. Format: STATES, INITIAL_STATE, and a nonempty FINAL_STATES header are present; FINAL_STATES: u0 is declared and is the correct accepting state (no pending obligation); every state has an explicit guard plus an else self-loop; guards are predicate-only using the given proposition ids. Reward safety: rewards are bounded and exploit-free — the +1.0 is reachable only through a preceding -1.0, so cumulative reward never exceeds 0 and no oscillation loop can farm reward. Reachability and compactness: both states are reachable (u1 via picking up the ball before the key, which is always possible), and two states is minimal for a pending-obligation property. Non-defect note: under the literal reading, the environment's canonical solve (dropping the key after opening the door while the ball stays aside, then grabbing the box) ends in u1 and is penalized; this is consistent with the task as written, and the task remains satisfiable (e.g., re-block the door cell and re-pick up the key before the final box grab, or never move the ball). No rewrite needed.

feedback: All checks pass. Function set: exactly the five environment-declared propositions (blocker_moved, has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost) — no extras, none missing; key_lost is declared even though the RM never references it, so defining it is required, and it is present. blocker_moved reproduces the documented door-relative read: for the single door at (dx, dy) it checks the cell (dx-1, dy) with a None-guard and type=='ball' test, so it is true exactly when no ball sits in front of the door (a ball in hand counts, since carried objects are off-grid), and it is a state read that turns false again if the ball is dropped back there — matching the non-latch condition semantics and the dx-1 offset documented in the code notes. has_door_key matches the documented expression exactly (carrying a key whose color equals some door's color). door_open matches exactly (any open door, is_open guarded). target_picked_up matches exactly (carrying a box whose color matches the mission string, no fixed color assumed). key_lost has correct event semantics: previous_valuation['has_door_key'] true at the previous step AND the current has_door_key expression false AND the current door_open expression false, with K and D textually identical to the standalone predicates; it reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read-only, never writes it, and the defensive truthiness guard plus 'not not' coercion yields a proper False at the first step and a bool in all cases. Persistent predicates read only current state; the event predicate only compares against the read-only snapshot. No imports, no actions, no side effects, no mutation of env or episode memory; all API usage (env.mission, env.carrying, env.grid.get, env.width, env.height) is within the documented scope, every grid read is None-guarded before attribute access, short-circuiting protects env.carrying dereferences, and syntax is valid executable Python. Consistent with the declared constraints (key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open by construction).
